- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.05) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5σ above historical mean, reduce by 0.1–0.3 units per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 0.5–1.0 unit lag correction if sentiment is bullish and price is trending up.
- If sentiment is neutral (±0.05) and price is volatile, reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
